title: Am I doomed ? or should I keep building -  2.5D Tactical RPG
author: PhaseConsistent3844
selftext:
The game harness I developed uses ML ensembles to classify a 2d environment into a fully playable scene, vibing with the era of prerendered games like FF8/9 . Which i'm really nostalgic about. 

Would love to hear feedback on whether you think this is tenable in the long run.   
Would you play a full game?  
To play free [https://perspectives.itch.io/varnmoor](https://perspectives.itch.io/varnmoor)

replies.author: PhaseConsistent3844
replies.body:
I wrote the story and the characters then used different harnesses for different things. I used meshy for models and gemini for  environments. Then a lot of non gen-ai models classify the scene and make it usable in a game engine. music is from Suno. 

Took a lot of trial and error and refining and there's still more to do in this department

replies.body: ok so if you go to the boat, there's a default option to get into a fight with the crew in the dialogue. Would love your feedback on this if you can! just go towards the water, find the boat, and attack!

replies.author: Xinnobun
replies.body:
Ok i tried it again the 2nd time. Went to a boat, spoke to Iron Kael, and then was trapped in a dialogue loop with no end.... Ended up closing the browser. 

I would cut down on some areas or at least add more to an area than just empty npc dialogues so people don't lose interest in your game so quickly. Like add interactives, more chests, barrels to collect coin etc.   
Being able to travel around in a town is nice but when the town is too big, it becomes a labyrinth and a nuissance. A lot of people just like to get to the point.

comments.author: AcanthisittaAware870
comments.body: Honestly it needs more work, you need to learn tools and techniques instead using meshy and other ai tools, you will only end up spending money to the A.I companies without making any profit.

replies.author: PhaseConsistent3844
replies.body: any direction in particular? ty any feedback is useful. atm this is a technical demo but I just decided to make it playable to build a bit in public

replies.author: AcanthisittaAware870
replies.body: I would recommend you start learning, hard surface modeling then trimsheets, tiles textures in blender and substance painter, move up to rigging, then sculpting characters, and animating, this should be able to give you more flexibility and power, you won't have to wait for ai to make you a chair, not knowing what to do with it.

replies.author: PhaseConsistent3844
replies.body: Are you essentially saying the 3D on 2D is a dead end? / not gonna work?

replies.author: Ferniclestix
replies.body:
Man If you dont already know that stuff its like 2 years.   
you shouldn't need to learn the modelling stuff.  dudes trolling you saying stuff like that.

all you really need is to get your AI to make you a little program that can load up your character with a skeleton,  then get it to create a list of animations and play them on loop when you tell it to.   then add a timeline with 'keyframes'   if you then go in to your skeleton you can make adjustments to the bones to make your animations hit better, give them hesitation, secondary action (thats like when things jiggle after impacts)  

really tho, i think mostly you just need more idle animations and some wandering logic so they dont stand there dead eyed.

replies.author: AcanthisittaAware870
replies.body: I am not trolling him at all, you don't seem to understand what i am saying, learn modeling it's easy than you think, you can learn it in a weekendz people think it's takes a lot of time,it doesn't.

replies.author: Ferniclestix
replies.body:
I understand it, im a 3d artist/animator. im saying he doesnt even need to go that far. AI is genuinely ok at making 3d models.  its not great at animation yet.  
if he wants to be better than the AI he needs at least a couple of months of tutorials and learning.  


im saying asking him to pick up all that stuff and just do it yourself is a bit much if hes not that way inclined already.

replies.author: AcanthisittaAware870
replies.body: The problem with AI 3d models are the mesh itself, currently they produce textures that look like geometry but no geometry below, and if you try to reduce the poly count, then there are problems with texturing or otherwise rigging which will take more time to fix than doing it from scratch.

replies.author: AcanthisittaAware870
replies.body: It's not a dead end, it's not difficult at all, what I am saying is of you learn things to you will produce actually results that people will play, AI is not capable for it currently.

replies.author: AcanthisittaAware870
replies.body: You don't need to learn all of tools and techniques, you only need to learn what's usefull for your usecase, you get what I am saying right?

comments.author: LiquidZebra
comments.body:
My dude, why are you mixing D&D and show 40% hit against AC18 if you need to manually time every hit? Is that one of those FF quick time event things?   
  
To me this is such an offputting mechanic.

replies.author: PhaseConsistent3844
replies.body: So I brought the quicktime hit as a bonus to hit and a bonus to damage to make battle a bit more action-based/engaging. Especially because there's no wizard shizzle/AOE hits yet in the game yet. Sorry it doesn't work for you. I'll keep in mind to make it optional. **But it's a bonus not a replacement for your stats.**

comments.author: No-Volume6352
comments.body:
I gave it a try! Being dropped straight onto the map without much context was a bit abrupt, so I just rolled with it and started exploring. That *Final Fantasy IX*-style approach is a great way to pull off a charming 3D-like map on a low budget—I’ve always thought it’s a solid technique that definitely isn’t outdated.  

The core combat system feels solid enough, too. It reminds me a lot of the *Arc the Lad* series. I’ve actually thought about making a game with a system like this myself, so it’s really cool to see someone actually building it.  

That said, tactical RPGs already tend to be a bit slow-paced by nature, so having QTE-style prompts pop up every single time might rub players the wrong way. I also think it really needs a lot more "juice" (game feel) to make the actions pop.  

Since I'm Japanese, I was mostly guessing my way through the English text, and I ended up getting wiped out as soon as I reached the ship with my starting gear. It’s a bit hard to tell whether the intended difficulty is closer to *Dark Souls* or a classic JRPG.

replies.author: PhaseConsistent3844
replies.body: hey there, The intended difficulty usually is reduced via your engagement in the quest. I try to make it so that you can butthead directly if you want but it makes the game maybe 2-3x harder than doing it 'the smooth way'/engaging with the quest.

comments.author: Any_Candle_6953
comments.body: The video looks nice! It looks like my type of game! I will give it a play and let you know my thoughts!

replies.author: Any_Candle_6953
replies.body:
\- I really like the look of the map!   
\- I definitely like the RPG elements of the dice rolls! Question: are you going to get in any legal trouble for that mechanic?  
\- I have no idea where to go or what to do. Some guidance is necessary--hugely necessary, especially in a tutorial/testing stage. The journal is next to useless with no context.  
\- I wasn't able to playtest combat in the time I spent playing before I had to go to work. I spent approximately 20 minutes playing, and explored what I believe to be most of the map. (the docks, the ship, the governor's hall, the tavern, one house)

Do I think it's tenable? Absolutely! It's neat to run around, and I imagine if I can customize my character I'd be even more into it. As far as "should you spend more time working on it" I guess that depends on what you want out of it. Are you having fun making it? Would you be happy with it even if no one played it?
